To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Deep convolutional neural networks can be learned with identification verification signal; (2) DeepID2+ has high recognition accuracy, which is the best reported to date; (3) Its hidden representations are sparse, and selective; (4) It is robust to occlusions.
deep convolutional networks are highly selective and robust to occlusion.
deep neural networks can learn to recognize faces with a very high level of accuracy and can learn to identify attributes that are not explicitly included in training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of the deep representations, which may shed light on the future design of face recognition systems.
understanding the representation power of deep convolutional nets, which is critical for the success of the face recognition system.
the properties of deep representations learned by a deep net for face recognition, which are not explicitly learned during the training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a deep net with high recognition accuracy is sparse, selective, robust, and can be trained with a simple identification-verification signal.
DeepID2+, which is learned with a simple identification/verification loss function, has implicitly acquired the ability to distinguish identities and attributes, and it is robust to occlusions.
the learned representations of DeepID2+ are highly discriminative, sparse, selective, robust and compact, and that the high performance is a direct result of these properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a deep neural network can be learned with a simple identification verification signal, and the learned representations are sparse, selectives and robust.

a well designed deep neural network with a large hidden representation space and a good training strategy can achieve high accuracy on face recognition, and it can learn a sparse, selective and robust representation for face images.
DeepID2+, as an example of deep convolutional networks, can learn high level concepts from data and generalize to unseen patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep convolutional nets are able to learn a compact representation of the face that is robust and selective to identity.
deep nets can learn discriminative representations with high sparsity, selectivity and robustness, even when they are not specifically trained to do so.
a good face representation should be sparse, selective and robust.
